Text is the page's main content; set full_page for every section, such as opening hours or fee tables. A js_required error means the page needs js: true; blocked means the site refused or showed a bot check. Preferred over web-crawl for new integrations. API docs: https://www.desearch.ai/docs/api-reference/get-web-extract

tools.name: search-api
tools.description: Web search on the Desearch index (POST /search). Returns ranked pages, each with its title, URL, publication date when known, and the passage that best matches the query. Set summary: true for a short answer written from the results with numbered citations; [n] in summary.text refers to summary.citations[].index. Set page_text to add each page's full text. Returns { summary, results, meta, cost_usd, usage_count, service, currency }, with summary first when requested; summary is null and meta.notices says 'Summary unavailable.' when it could not be written. Use search for titles and links only, and web-search for SERP-style snippets.

query.description: Search query, example: 'Who won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics?'

mode.description: 'fast' returns results sooner; 'balanced' (API default) favors relevance.

start_date.description: Only pages published on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

end_date.description: Only pages published on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

highlights.description: Include the passage that best matches the query (API default true).

page_text.description: Include each page's full text (API default false).

exclude_domains.description: Never pages on these domains or their subdomains (at most 1,200). Wins over include_domains and site:.

summary.description: Also return a short answer written from the results, with numbered citations (API default false). No extra charge.

tools.name: tiktok
tools.description: Read public TikTok data with Desearch. Set action and that action's arguments. search (query; optional count, sort, cursor): videos that match a keyword. post (id): one video by its ID. profile (username): one profile. profile_posts (username; optional count, cursor): a user's videos. comments (video_id; optional count, cursor): a video's comments. hashtag (tag; optional count, cursor): videos with a hashtag. trending (optional region, count): trending videos for a region, one page. A video id from search can be passed to post or comments. post and profile return the item itself. List actions return { results, next_cursor, next }. For the next page, call again with the same action and target and cursor set to next_cursor, unchanged; next_cursor is null on the last page. A cursor lasts 24 hours.

tag.description: hashtag: the hashtag without #, example: 'ai'. A leading # is removed.

region.description: trending: two-letter region code, example: 'US' (API default).

tools.name: people-search
tools.description: Start a paid job billed to the user's Desearch balance: find people on X, YouTube, LinkedIn, or TikTok who match a plain-language description. Returns a task_id at once, with the task's status and reserved_cost_usd. Cost: the call reserves count times the platform's per-person price at the time of the call (reserved_cost_usd; prices at https://desearch.ai/pricing). When the search ends you pay only for the people it delivered (final_cost_usd; a per-search minimum applies when it finds anyone; a search that finds no one is free) and the rest of the reservation is returned. Data: each person comes back with a fit score, why they matched, their audience, and only the contacts and links they list publicly. Desearch reads public data only. X: public posts and public profile fields (bio, followers, website, location). YouTube: public channel pages (About section, subscribers, country, links) and the creator's own website for publicly listed contact details. LinkedIn: public posts and public profiles (headline, company, location, followers, about). TikTok: public videos and public profiles (bio, followers, likes, latest videos, a public email listed in the bio). People found stay readable for 30 days after the search ends. The search runs in the background, usually for 1 to 5 minutes: poll people-search-status with the task_id to read progress and the people found so far, and use people-search-pause, people-search-resume, or people-search-cancel to pause, resume, or cancel it. Do not start the same search twice; send idempotency_key so a retry returns the first task instead of charging again. Filters depend on the platform. x: min_followers, max_followers, verified_only, countries, keywords, exclude_keywords. youtube: min_subscribers, max_subscribers, countries, require_contact, keywords, exclude_keywords. linkedin: min_followers, max_followers, countries, keywords, exclude_keywords. tiktok: min_followers, max_followers, require_contact, keywords, exclude_keywords.

platform.description: Where to look: 'x' (X profiles), 'youtube' (YouTube creators), 'linkedin' (LinkedIn members), or 'tiktok' (TikTok creators).

query.description: Who you are looking for, in plain language, example: 'Skincare creators who review sunscreen'.

count.description: How many qualified people to find (5-200, API default 25). The search reserves this many and bills only the people it delivers.

min_score.description: Only return people with at least this fit score (0-100).

exclude.description: Handles to leave out, for example people you already contacted.

idempotency_key.description: Any unique string for this search, for example a UUID. Sending the same key again returns the first task and is not charged again.

metadata.description: Your own labels for this search, example: {"campaign": "q4-outbound"}. Up to 10 keys; keys are 1-40 characters of a-z, 0-9, '_', '.', '-'; values are strings of up to 200 characters. Returned on the task; filter people-search-tasks by it. The search does not use it.

min_followers.description: Minimum follower count. x, linkedin, tiktok.

max_followers.description: Maximum follower count. x, linkedin, tiktok.

verified_only.description: Only verified or X Premium accounts. x only.

require_contact.description: Only creators with a public email (tiktok: in the bio; youtube: an email or contact link). youtube, tiktok.

countries.description: Countries to prefer, example: ['US', 'GB']. x, youtube, linkedin.

keywords.description: Words that should appear in their posts, videos, or bio. All platforms.

exclude_keywords.description: Leave out people who mention these words. All platforms.

tools.name: people-search-status
tools.description: Status, progress, and cost of one People Search task, plus a page of the people found so far: name, handle, url, platform, audience, location, fit score, why they matched, contacts, and links. Free: it reads a search you already started and runs no new search. Cost fields are reserved_cost_usd and, once the search ended, final_cost_usd. People come from public profiles and posts on the search's platform, with only the contacts they list publicly. People arrive while the search runs: pass the returned next_cursor as cursor on the next call to get only the people found since then. When done is true and has_more is false you have everyone the search found. An ended task has completion_reason (why it stopped), coverage_limited: true when a budget stopped it before count (more people may match), and warnings such as partial_enrichment (some profiles could not be read, so those people were scored on the search hit; they show enrichment: failed). Each person has fully_verified (every criterion confirmed by their own profile or posts) and unverified_criteria (criteria that are unknown or not met, or a disqualifier that applies). These are information only: the person still qualified.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous people-search-status call. Omit to start from the first person.

include_people.description: Set false to read only the status, progress, and cost.

tools.name: people-search-pause
tools.description: Pause a People Search task and return its updated status. Free: it charges and refunds nothing. A queued search pauses at once; a running one finishes its current batch first (status pausing, then paused). Pausing loses no data: the people found so far stay readable with people-search-status, and the search keeps its progress. Billing does not change: the reservation made when the search started stays reserved while paused and is settled only when the search ends. Undo it with people-search-resume, which continues from where the search stopped with no new charge. Limit: a search paused for more than 7 days is cancelled by the API and can no longer be resumed; you then pay only for the people already delivered, the rest of the reservation is returned, and the people found stay readable for 30 days.

tools.name: people-search-resume
tools.description: Resume a paused People Search task and return its updated status. Free. The search continues from where it stopped, keeping the people already found, with no new charge: the cost already spent is carried forward and the original reservation still covers it. Works only on a paused search, within 7 days of pausing; a search in any other state, including one the API cancelled after 7 days paused, returns 409. Poll people-search-status for the new people.

tools.name: people-search-cancel
tools.description: Cancel a People Search task. Free. The search stops for good; you pay only for the people it already delivered and the rest of the reservation is returned. People found so far stay readable for 30 days. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: people-search-tasks
tools.description: Your People Search tasks, newest first, with status, counts, cost, why each ended search stopped (completion_reason, coverage_limited), and the metadata labels set on people-search. Free; it lists your own tasks, not the people they found (read those with people-search-status or people-profiles). Use it to find a task_id (filter by metadata to find the searches of one campaign), or to see which searches are still queued, running, or paused: a new search is refused while too many are active.

platform.description: Only tasks on this platform: 'x', 'youtube', 'linkedin', or 'tiktok'.

status.description: Only tasks in these statuses, example: ['running', 'paused'].

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Keep the same metadata filter when you page.

metadata.description: Only tasks whose metadata has all of these key/value pairs (exact match, up to 3), example: {"campaign": "q4-outbound"}.

tools.name: people-profiles
tools.description: Everyone your own People Searches found on one platform, one entry per person: their best-scoring result (name, handle, url, audience, location, fit score, why they matched, public contacts, and links) and the search that found them (found_by). Free: it reads only people your earlier searches found, runs no new search, and queries no outside source. That data came from public profiles and posts, with only the contacts each person lists publicly. Search by name, handle, bio, or location with q, filter by contact channels (has), audience, fit score, location, or verification, and sort by score, recent, or audience. People from searches that ended more than 30 days ago are left out.

q.description: Text in the name, handle, bio, or location, example: 'skincare'.

has.description: Channels every person must have, example: ['email', 'instagram']. 'email' is a public email; the others are a link of that type.

location.description: Text in the location, example: 'united states'.

verified.description: Only verified accounts. Only X and TikTok people carry a verified flag.

tools.description: The people your own People Searches found, as CSV or JSON Lines text: one search (task_id), or everyone found on one platform (platform, with the same q, sort, and filters as people-profiles). The reply is a note with the row count, then the file text cut at a row boundary to max_rows rows and 50,000 characters; the note says how many rows were cut and where to get the whole file. CSV keeps its header row. The data came from public profiles and posts, with only the contacts each person lists publicly.

platform.description: Without task_id: export everyone found on 'x', 'youtube', 'linkedin', or 'tiktok'.

q.description: Platform export only: text in the name, handle, bio, or location.

has.description: Channels every person must have, example: ['email']. 'email' is a public email; the others are a link of that type.

location.description: Text in the location, example: 'united states'.

verified.description: Only verified accounts. Only X and TikTok people carry a verified flag.

max_rows.description: Most rows to return (1-1000, default 100). The reply also stops before 50,000 characters of file text.

tools.name: company-search
tools.description: Start a paid job billed to the user's Desearch balance: find companies on the web that match a plain-language description, and collect each one's public contact data. Returns a task_id at once, with the task's status and reserved_cost_usd. Cost: without max_cost_usd, the call reserves count companies at the Company Search per-company price at the time of the call (reserved_cost_usd; prices at https://desearch.ai/pricing). When the task ends you pay only for the companies it delivered (final_cost_usd; a minimum of 1 when it delivers any; a task that delivers none is free) and the rest of the reservation is returned. A company left out by min_score or require is not billed. Such a search stops once it costs more than the companies it found pay for (completion_reason cost_limit, coverage_limited: true). Search budget: with max_cost_usd the whole budget is reserved, and the search goes on until it delivers count or spends the budget. Its search effort is billed where the companies delivered do not cover it, up to the budget, even when it finds few companies or none; the unused part is returned. Set max_cost_usd only when the user agreed to spend that amount, never on your own. Find more: when a search ended before count because a limit stopped it (coverage_limited, for example cost_limit), offer the user a new company-search with the same query and filters, continue_from set to its task_id, and count set to the companies still wanted, optionally with a budget the user agrees to. It leaves out every company the earlier search delivered or held for review, so it finds only new ones. To check only companies you name, give their websites in query, for example 'Restrict this search to Acme (acme.com.au) and Beta (beta.co.uk). Return only those.' Only those domains are then checked against the rest of the description, with no web search (the task shows them as only_domains and ends with completion_reason all_domains_processed). Companies named without their websites do not restrict the search (warning scope_not_applied). Each company has a fit score (0-100) and why it matched, plus fully_verified and unverified_criteria (what its own pages do and do not confirm). Data: Desearch reads public data only: each company's own website (its homepage and its contact, about, team, and imprint pages), public web search results, and public LinkedIn profiles of its leaders. Each company comes back with its location, public emails, phones, and social profiles, and its leaders (roles) with their title, LinkedIn profile, and emails. Every contact keeps the page it came from (source_url). Leader emails can be inferred from the company's address pattern (source: inferred, with a confidence), and every email is checked (verification: valid, invalid, risky, or unknown). Companies stay readable for 30 days after the task ends. The task runs in the background: poll company-search-status with the task_id to read progress and the companies delivered so far. Each company is delivered first with enrichment status partial, and the later stages (contact pages, leaders, inferred emails, email checks) fill it in until it is complete. Use company-search-pause, company-search-resume, or company-search-cancel to pause, resume, or cancel it. Do not start the same task twice; send idempotency_key so a retry returns the first task instead of charging again. To read companies you already know by domain, use company-enrich instead.

query.description: The companies you are looking for, in plain language: what they do, where, how far along. Example: 'Series A fintech startups in Berlin building payment infrastructure'. Returns the monitor (monitor_id, settings, max_run_cost_usd, next_run_at) and, when webhook_url is set, webhook_secret, which is shown only here. With run_now (the API default) the first run is queued at once and billed when it ends; set run_now false to wait for the schedule. Creating, reading, changing, and deleting monitors is free. Each run is billed when it ends: its searches at their list price (TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, and Meta ads per read, $3.00 per 1,000 reads ($0.003 a read), whatever the number of posts: one read per watched account, hashtag, or Facebook page, per TikTok keyword search, and per Ad Library search; an empty or private TikTok account takes two reads, so the hold counts two per TikTok account; a watched X account about $0.003, its 20-post timeline; a watched subreddit, YouTube channel, or Threads account $0.00207 each; ten watched accounts cost about ten searches), AI screening at $0.05 per 1,000 new items screened, and the summary's LLM usage plus 50% when summary is on. A run with no new items still pays for its searches. While a run is queued or running, its most (max_run_cost_usd) is held on the balance; it is billed what it used and the rest is released. A run that cannot be held fails with insufficient_credits and pauses the monitor. Use monitor-estimate for the cost of a configuration. Each run searches its sources inside a window that starts where the previous run ended (or, for a source with watched accounts or hashtags, reads each feed's newest posts), drops everything the monitor has already seen, and screens the new items with an AI classifier: relevant (about what the query watches), new_info (news rather than an evergreen page), and one yes/no question per criterion. score is the lowest of relevant and the criteria x 100; an item is kept at min_score (0 keeps every new post). Read kept items with monitor-items or monitor-run; with a webhook they are also POSTed to it, signed with webhook_secret. TikTok search has no working date filter and ranks by relevance, so a TikTok keyword monitor finds a new video only when it reaches TikTok's top results; to follow creators or a tag, watch their accounts (tiktok_accounts) or the hashtag (tiktok_hashtags). 'instagram' and 'facebook' have no keyword search: they read only watched feeds, so a monitor with 'instagram' needs instagram_accounts or instagram_hashtags and one with 'facebook' needs facebook_pages, or the API answers 422. Facebook has no organic hashtag feed. 'meta_ads' searches the Meta Ad Library with the query, so write the query as keywords (a brand, product, or short phrase such as 'ChatGPT'); a sentence finds nothing. An ad counts as new the first time a run sees it if it started within the last 30 days, and ads are screened with their own relevance question and no new_info. Threads keyword search returns loosely matched posts, so watch accounts there (threads_accounts). Limits: 25 monitors per account (409 too_many_monitors); 402 when the balance cannot hold one run, even with run_now false.

query.description: What to watch, in plain words (3-500 characters). Each source is searched with it. Example: 'Bittensor subnet launches and updates'. With 'meta_ads', use keywords (a brand, product, or short phrase such as 'ChatGPT'): the Ad Library finds nothing for a sentence.
